newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Coconut Oil-Prices seen mixed on stocks prospects.
newsitem.headline: Coconut Oil-Prices seen mixed on stocks prospects.

text.p: Coconut oil prices are expected to be mixed this week, reflecting supply prospects in Europe and the U.S., Manila traders said on Monday.
"I expect coconut oil prices for nearby months to remain steady to higher this week despite fresh stocks from MV Kenwood Park," said one dealer.
"The scenario for forward months, however, is a different ballgame. Prices for February/March deliveries would be softer due to prospects of more deliveries," the trader added.
Coconut oil prices for November/December shipments were expected to rise by $30 to $850 per tonne CIF from the last traded price of $820, another trader said.
Shipments for January/February were expected to rise by $7.50 to $780 per tonne CIF, he said.
Traders said prices for February/March shipments should come down by at least $5 per tonne from a current level of $750 to $760 per tonne CIF.
The arrival of the Kenwood Park with a cargo of between 30,000 and 38,000 tonnes for the European and U.S. markets last week boosted stocks in Rotterdam to 34,000 tonnes, Manila traders said.
December demand for coconut oil in Europe was put by Philippine traders at 55,000 tonnes.
Traders also said current stocks in the U.S. were below monthly requirements of 45,000 tonnes.
"We don't expect any more improvement in the current stocks in Europe and the U.S. markets as MV Kenwood Park was the last big ship carrying coconut oil for the month," one trader said.
The Stolt Sapphire, with a cargo of 3,000 tonnes of coconut oil, left the country on November 6 and was scheduled to arrive at Rotterdam on December 21.
The next big shipment for the U.S. and European markets was due to arrive in Rotterdam on January 5, 1997, with a cargo of 28,000 tonnes.
Another ship, the Auriga, with a cargo of 27,000 tonnes of coconut oil, was scheduled to leave the country next week.
The ship would dock at Rotterdam in late January, a trader at one of the country's largest commodity firms said.
